author: nshchego
title: OpenVINO JS Electron E2E test fails: fetch failed downloading Electron binary via @electron/get
signature: TypeError: fetch failed during @electron/get FetchDownloader.download while npm install demo-electron-app-project runs 'npm start' E2E Electron dependency test; Electron binary failed to install correctly|Network

failed_jobs.name: OpenVINO JS API (22) / OpenVINO JS API
failed_jobs.symptom: E2E of openvino-node package: 'should run electron package and verify output' fails because Electron binary could not be downloaded (fetch failed)

root_cause: The 'OpenVINO JS API (22)' job (ARM64 shard) runs the demo-electron-app-project E2E test, which triggers 'npm install' followed by 'npm start'. During install, Electron's postinstall script (via @electron/get's FetchDownloader) attempts to download the prebuilt Electron binary over HTTPS from the GitHub releases CDN. This download raised 'TypeError: fetch failed' (an undici-level network error), leaving node_modules/electron without its downloaded binary. When 'npm start' subsequently tried to launch Electron, index.js's getElectronPath() detected the missing binary and threw 'Electron failed to install correctly'. The merged commit (PR #39469, by nshchego) only modifies GPU plugin C++ code (fully_connected_onednn.cpp/hpp) for oneDNN decompression-group handling and is completely unrelated to the JS bindings or Electron tooling, confirming this is an external network/CDN flake rather than a regression introduced by the commit.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible locally; depends on transient network/CDN failures. To approximate: cd src/bindings/js/node, set up demo-electron-app-project, run 'npm install' repeatedly on a constrained/unstable network connection (or temporarily block access to the Electron binary download host) to observe the same 'fetch failed' / 'Electron failed to install correctly' error chain.
recommended_actions: Add retry logic around the Electron binary download step (e.g., set the ELECTRON_GET_USE_PROXY / npm config electron_config_cache, or wrap 'npm install' with a retry wrapper) in the E2E Electron test setup.
Consider caching the downloaded Electron binary across CI runs (e.g., actions/cache keyed on Electron version) to avoid repeated cold downloads that are exposed to transient network failures.
Add a short automatic retry (2-3 attempts) specifically for the Electron E2E job before marking it failed, since this is a known external dependency flake class distinct from code regressions.
Optionally pin/vendor a mirror or internal artifact proxy for the Electron binary download to reduce dependency on the public CDN's availability from ARM64 runners.
prevention_strategies: Treat Electron/@electron/get binary downloads as an external-service dependency prone to transient network failures; add retries and/or local caching for this download step, and ensure the E2E Electron test categorizes a download failure distinctly from an actual OpenVINO/Electron integration regression so reviewers are not misled about code health.
historical_context: A related but distinct pattern was previously recorded: pattern 09126916fe54469f ('npm install timeout in electron e2e test due to npm registry audit endpoint 503') on 2026-10-22, where 'npm install' itself stalled on the npm registry's audit endpoint. The current failure is different: npm install completed, but the Electron binary download via @electron/get failed with a generic fetch error during the postinstall step. Both point to the same underlying fragility: the demo-electron-app-project E2E test has multiple external-network dependencies (npm registry, Electron binary CDN) with no caching or retry, making it the most network-flake-prone job in the JS API test suite.
